Always use a kettle with an auto-shutoff so it never boils dry or overheats.
Keep kettle handles turned inward, away from the stove edge, to avoid accidental knocks.
Never leave boiling water or a hot kettle unattended while it heats.
Fill the kettle only to the marked maximum line to prevent splashing overflow.
Test the temperature with the back of your hand before lifting a steaming cup.
Set hot drinks on a stable, flat, non-slip surface so they cannot topple.
Use mugs with heat-safe handles and always grip the handle, not the body.
Pour hot water slowly and steadily to avoid splashes and steam burns.
Keep young children and pets away from the counter while hot water is out.
Place a teapot or kettle away from table and counter edges.
Wear long sleeves or use a towel mitt when handling a very hot pot.
Never carry a full cup of hot water while walking quickly or on stairs.
Screw thermos and flask lids tight before carrying, and check they feel secure.
Use a trivet or heat mat to protect surfaces and prevent skidding.
Never microwave water in containers you cannot safely lift.
Open steam vents and lids away from your face to avoid steam burns.
Give piping-hot drinks a minute to cool before taking a first sip.
Teach children to ask an adult before touching anything that held hot water.
Unplug the kettle immediately after the water boils.
Position the kettle cord so nothing and no one can trip over it near hot water.
Use tongs or a mitt to remove a boiled egg or item from hot water.
Warning stickers: remind yourself the cup is still hot even after it stops steaming.
Never refill a mug with hot water on the same spot a spill just happened.
Drain hot water from pots slowly to avoid sudden steam bursts.
Keep paper towels and cloth napkins away from open flames near the stove.
If your hands are wet or soapy, dry them before touching a hot handle.
Put a rubber mat in the sink so hot rinsing water can't splash your legs.
Rinse a burned area with cool, not cold or hot, running water for relief.
Store hot water thermoses out of reach of small children after use.
When unsure if something is still hot, touch it gently with a knuckle, not a palm.
